runs.question: Query the first-seen block arrival times for mainnet blocks on 20 June 2026 (UTC).
runs.answer:
[Turn 1 | session=ses_08faae173ffeaH0LImUXCIA53r] Query the first-seen block arrival times for mainnet blocks on 20 June 2026 (UTC).
The query returned **7,200 rows** (one per slot) from `mainnet.fct_block_first_seen_by_node` for 20 June 2026. Each row has:

- **slot** / **slot_start_date_time** — the block slot and its wall-clock time (UTC)
- **arrival_time_ms** — the minimum `seen_slot_start_diff` (ms) across all observing nodes, i.e. the fastest first-seen arrival
- **observations** — how many nodes reported seeing that block (typically 156–158)

The range covers slot **14,590,799** (`00:00:11`) through **14,597,998** (`23:59:59`). Arrival times vary from as low as **215 ms** (slot 14,597,916) up to ~**3,725 ms** (slot 14,597,760), with typical values around **1,200–1,600 ms**.

[Turn 2 | session=ses_08faae173ffeaH0LImUXCIA53r] Plot the distribution of those arrival times as a chart.
Chart generated and uploaded:

- **URL:** http://127.0.0.1:2480/api/v1/storage/files/54c41622c9c5/e965cb9f-3437-4d8b-89f8-584e8f8ac1e1/arrival_histogram.png
- **Host path:** /home/runner/.panda/data/storage/54c41622c9c5/e965cb9f-3437-4d8b-89f8-584e8f8ac1e1/arrival_histogram.png

The histogram shows the distribution of per-slot minimum first-seen arrival times (in ms) across all mainnet blocks on 20 June 2026, with the bulk clustering in the ~1,000–2,000 ms range.
